transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because... I just can't shake this thought I've been having. I've been an electrician for years, and if all my experience couldn't keep my own brother safe, then... I just feel like I'm a danger to anybody who works with me, or even the people living under my roof.
Do you find yourself performing any specific rituals or repetitive actions to try to neutralize these thoughts or prevent the harm you fear?

No, I don't do anything like that. I mean, I don't have any rituals or... repeat things over and over to try and make it go away, if that's what you mean. The thoughts just kind of stay there in my head, and I just have to sit with them. I don't really do anything special to try and stop them.
Did these thoughts begin following a specific, distressing event involving your brother?
Yeah, they did. Um, this has all been going on for about four months now. It started right after the garage fire... and ever since my nephew came to live with us.
Do you find yourself having vivid, intrusive memories or nightmares about the garage fire?

Yeah, I do. It's... it's bad. I'll be right in the middle of wiring a panel at work, or even just sitting at home and I hear my nephew shut the garage door, and suddenly... it's like the whole job site or the house just drops out from under me. I'm right back there. I can smell the smoke. I can see my brother. It just hits me out of nowhere and it feels like it's happening all over again.
Since the fire, have you been going out of your way to avoid certain places, people, or activities that remind you of what happened?

Yeah, I have. I actually avoid my own garage now—I won't go in there unless I absolutely have to. I also quit helping out with the electrical stuff at my church. I just can't do it right now. And if anyone starts talking about car projects, or tries to bring up the fire... I just shut them down fast. I don't want to talk about it, and I don't want to be around anything that reminds me of it.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood or energy levels, such as feeling constantly on edge, having trouble sleeping, or finding it difficult to concentrate?

Yeah, my sleep has been really bad. Most nights, I just lie there in the dark. I'm constantly listening for any little noise... like a crackling sound, or a car door shutting out in the driveway. And when I finally do manage to fall asleep, it doesn't last. I'll jolt awake, just completely soaked in sweat from dreaming about the garage. Once that happens, I can't get back to sleep before my alarm goes off for work. So, yeah, I'm definitely having trouble sleeping.
